messages:
oncall-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: Incident P-1221 - High DNS resolver error rate (geo-dns) in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. Paging vikram (SRE oncall).
vikram: got it, picking up. seeing a spike in 5xx from our edge resolvers? any customer reports?
carmen: support ticket queue just started filling, a handful of apps reporting timeouts to embeddings.redwood.ai in EU. NB: minimal errors from US.
sam: monitoring: resolver error rate ~18% in eu-west-1, eu-central ~22% for the last 12m. Route53 health checks show increased latencies for our regional glue records.
netty: Cloudflare probe telemetry indicates intermittent NXDOMAINs and SERVFAILs hitting 1-3 of their resolver clusters in EU. Could be an upstream resolver flap.
vikram: running quick dig to reproduce from within eu2-pooled box:

```
$ dig +short @10.0.1.11 api.redwood-inference.net A
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```

vikram: traceroute to resolver IPs shows packet loss at CF edge hop.
carmen: customer impact: degraded for EU-read requests that prefer local region. Global fallback still okay but latency spikes due to inter-region routing.
sam: adding logs: fetching edge logs for 2687654*. Pattern: resolver errors correlate with 504s on our HTTP layer (upstream DNS failures -> backend name resolution timeout).
netty: confirmed: Cloudflare is reporting an internal resolver cluster recovery in progress (status page msg). Route53 not showing outages but TTL/prog suggests inconsistent propagation across geo-weights.
vikram: immediate mitigation options:
- 1) Switch geo-policy to prefer-us-backup for EU -> quick weight tweak in Route53 (fast, partial fix, may increase latency)
- 2) Force failover to secondary resolver pool (internal) via prefix policy (requires config push to edge daemons)
- 3) Push advisory to support + status page and wait for Cloudflare to resolve (non-invasive)

carmen: customers impacted are mid-to-large with EU-only deployments. I recommend option 1 as start and option 2 if it doesn't improve in 10m.
vikram: agree. I'll prepare a Route53 change: reduce EU weights from 90 -> 10 and increase backup region weight.
sam: watchlist: watch resolver error rate, http 5xx rate, and token auth failures (could be cascading). I'm opening a temporary dashboard.

oncall-bot: Deploy request logged: route53-change/2687654321 by vikram. Approve with :thumbsup: to proceed.
vikram: :thumbsup:
netty: note: pushing weight change may cause some clients to see a new IP quickly but others will honor old TTLs. we'll still see mixed traffic for ~TTL window.

vikram: executed Route53 change (change-id: C2687654321). command:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://eu-weight-shift.json --hosted-zone-id ZREDWOOD
```

sam: seeing initial drop in resolver errors in eu-west from 18% -> 6% within 90s. eu-central still high.
carmen: support: notifying affected customers with the summary + ETA for full recovery. posting incident note to status page.

support: status update posted: "Partial mitigation in place; routing adjusted to reduce reliance on affected resolver clusters. Monitoring."
vikram: still seeing edge traces showing intermittent Cloudflare SERVFAILs for a subset of prefixes. initiating fallback plan: trigger config push to edge-daemons to prefer internal-resolver-pool.
netty: config push queued. rollout 20% -> 100% over 5m.

oncall-bot: config-push job 9001 started by vikram. Progress updates will be posted.

sam: after first 20% rollout, eu-central resolver errors dropped from 22% -> 8%. HTTP 504s down ~60%.
carmen: good. escalate to SRE lead for awareness and handoff in 20m.

vikram: preparing handoff note for next oncall (end of shift). Summary:
- root cause: external resolver cluster flap at Cloudflare causing NX/SERVFAILs -> inconsistent GeoDNS resolution
- impact: elevated DNS errors and client timeouts for EU-preferring traffic, partial failover to US increased latency
- mitigations performed: Route53 weight shift -> reduced EU reliance; edge config push to internal resolver pool -> further improvement
- customer comms: status page update + targeted outreach ongoing
- next steps: monitor 3h, coordinate with Cloudflare support to correlate internal cluster failover logs, consider TTL reduction on affected records if recurrence.

pagerduty: Incident P-1221 acknowledged by sre-lead. Scheduled follow-up bridge at +30m.
vikram: handing off to codenext oncall: @sam you're primary after me, pls watch for regression and coordinate long-term mitigation with netty.
sam: ack. I'll take over and set a 30m checkpoint to assess return-to-normal.

oncall-bot: Incident P-1221 status: mitigated -> partial, postmortem_required: yes, severity: sev2. Thread closed for active mitigation; use #incidents for updates.
vikram: adding runbook note under incidents/geo-dns: add steps to prefer-internal-resolver and route53-weight-rollback snippet.

carmen: closing loop with support: we sent proactive emails to 5 affected customers, and we're tracking any lingering errors.
vikram: final: marking as handoff complete. leaving detailed logs and dig/traceroute outputs in the incident ticket.

sam: will follow up. thanks all. :tada:"
